reporting_issues.note: Tables 1 and 2 print an F-value column only; no degrees of freedom appear anywhere in the paper.
The percentages and the single kcal figure cannot be reconciled from the text, and the lower dose produced the larger percentage reduction.
The threshold is set on p. 77 without justification.
p. 76: three men began and did not complete, one of them reporting difficulty sleeping during the 10 mg phase.

The 'content' example is right (30.80 with SEM 0.07 in the placebo column), but 'dizzy' 0.00 with SEM 0.00 is the 10 mg methamphetamine value, not the placebo value: placebo was 4.96 (SEM 1.36), and a floor of zero on an active-drug row is unremarkable. A better second example from the placebo column is 'withdrawn', 11.04 with SEM 0.33.
Both tables are titled as showing the significant ratings only.

risk_of_bias.note: High is right and equals the worst domain (selection of the reported result). Design and instrument fit: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, within-person choice study with the two active doses counterbalanced is the case METHODS 5.3 names for RoB 2.

risk_of_bias_domains.note: Counterbalanced rather than randomized (p. 77), and the placebo conditions always followed their matched active condition on days 9-11 and 17-19.
Judgment is right. As on the Mendelson card, this is an added domain rather than one of RoB 2's five; the editor may prefer it folded into the randomization domain.
Double-blind, but every participant had taken an open 10 mg dose beforehand and capsule colour changed between conditions.
Three of eleven did not complete, one for a drug-related reason, and only completers are analysed.
Choices and bar-code food records validated against the daily waste; self-reports are the measure of interest.
A 50-item battery tabulated only where significant, psychomotor data not reported, food values only in a figure, F values without degrees of freedom, threshold P<0.03.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor is right: the reinforcement conclusion holds for this sample against a $1 alternative, and the three qualifications the card adds (stimulant-experienced rather than methamphetamine-experienced participants, the single alternative value, and ratings taken only after the sample dose) are all supported at the pages given.

missed: Count error in the outcomes field: Table 1 lists 23 items, 12 raised and 11 lowered, not 22.

Analysis exclusion not recorded: choices were also analysed by time of day, and morning choice data were left out of that analysis because the morning dose on the first day of each condition was the sample dose (p. 77).

Funding field: the acknowledgement on p. 80 prints the grant number alone; the attribution to the National Institute on Drug Abuse is the card's inference, correct for a DA- number but worth marking as inferred.
